## My Thinking

I have been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life — since I was a boy watching my father work. I am 63 now and my back is not what it was. I do not read, so I learn from watching neighbors and listening at the village seed shop. I have maybe 8 mu of flat land by the well.

There is only one way I know to farm here: wheat in the fall, corn after wheat. That is what my father did, what every family on this road does, what the grain buyers in town want. I am not going to try vegetables or something new at my age with no one to help me read the instructions.

For wheat, I will hire the tractor man to rotary-till before I plant in October. I will use the improved seed the shop sells — I do not know the name exactly but it is what Wang next door used and his yield was good. I put down diammonium phosphate when I plant, then urea in the spring when the wheat wakes up, then again at jointing. I pump from the well three times: before the ground freezes, at jointing, and at heading if the sky stays dry. I spray twice — once for weeds early on, once for aphids in May.

After I cut the wheat in June, I plant corn the same day with the seeder — no tilling, just straight in. Corn seed I always use hybrid, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the dealer says is similar. Summer has rain so I only pump once, maybe not at all. Two sprays for corn borer and weeds.

I expect around 450 jin per mu for wheat and maybe 550 for corn. Some years more, some less. That is life.
